report_text: The slide range 250‑256 provides a solid definition of DevOps and clearly states its primary objective of shortening the system development life cycle (SDLC). These points directly answer the first two student questions. However, the third question—why development and operations teams have historically had conflicting goals—is only touched on superficially. The slides note that the two groups have "different goals and incentives" and reference pre‑cloud manual processes, but they do not elaborate on the underlying reasons (e.g., developers prioritising rapid feature delivery versus operations prioritising stability, reliability, and cost). No additional slides in the immediate vicinity (including slide 257) expand on this historical tension. Consequently, the topic covers the conflict in name only, offering shallow coverage rather than a full explanatory narrative. To close this gap, a dedicated slide (or a brief expansion of the existing content) should outline the typical objectives of each discipline, the metrics that drove their separate incentives, and how these misaligned priorities manifested before the DevOps movement.
